title: POC Gate Interop & Creds Progress - weekly sync
summary: Quick weekly POC sync focusing on credential handoff, staging gateway interop tests, and a re-run of tail-latency microbenchmarks. SE recommends KV cache prewarming and a small quantization profile tweak to meet 95th percentile SLO. Next steps include producing a short runbook, sharing SOC2 + KMS notes, and scheduling a 2-hour perf window.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and KMS integration note by 2026-07-30
Customer to confirm service account creation and provide gateway IP allowlist by 2026-08-02
SE to run 2-hour tail-latency benchmark on 2026-08-04 and share results
AE to send updated pricing example and pilot commit options by 2026-07-31
transcript:
Meeting: POC Gate Interop & Creds Progress - weekly sync
Date: 2026-07-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (OrionFin Eng Lead), Luis Ramirez (OrionFin Infra), Tamara Okoye (OrionFin Security)

Summary: quick status, blocked items, proposed perf run, security checklist, next steps

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, should we do quick round robin on blockers, maybe start with creds and gateway?
[00:12] Priya Patel: yeah thanks Maya, we, uh, have service account created but the API key rotation policy in our org requires vault-backed keys, so we're waiting on infra to wire the allowlist and the vault role, luis?
[00:25] Luis Ramirez: yeah, um, PR is open, I need the gateway IP ranges from you, redwood, and I've got some terraform bits to finish. we tried a quick connect yesterday and saw TLS handshake errors intermittently.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: that sounds like SNI mismatch-ish, sometimes our staging gateway defaults to the older cert chain if the SNI header is missing, we'll share exact hostnames. also we saw the same TLS flake when the VPC peering had MTU set to 1400 in one of the clouds, so small packets could fragment.
[01:02] Tamara Okoye: from security side we need KMS integration details, audit log retention, and whether Redwood's control plane can be kept off our VPC (we prefer private control-plane). also SOC 2 type 2 evidence is on our checklist.
[01:20] Maya Chen: totally, we can provide SOC 2 artifacts and an integration note for KMS; for private control plane we have an option in Private deployment — we can detail network flows. i'll attach the doc after the call.
[01:33] Priya Patel: great. on the bench metrics, we re-ran the sample chat workload and saw tail latency spike at 95th to 420ms for a 512-token average request which is above our 300ms goal.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: thanks for those numbers, did you use batching and KV cache on?
[01:52] Priya Patel: KV cache was disabled; we were running cold for a couple tests.
[01:56] Jordan Lee: that explains it — enabling KV cache and a small prefix cache drastically reduces tail for repeated contexts. we recommend warming the cache with a short run. also there's a quant profile we can try, drop to q4_0 for embeddings path, might save tokens and cut latency by ~10% based on our internal evals.
[02:15] Luis Ramirez: curious about quantization tradeoffs — do you see any quality regression for our usecase (multi-turn financial assistant)?
[02:22] Jordan Lee: negligible for retrieval-augmented flows; we'll run diffs on your prompt set. if it's sensitive we can pin hosts to dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor variance.
[02:31] Priya Patel: dedicated is costlier; we'll need ballpark pricing.
[02:35] Maya Chen: i'll include a short pricing appendix for a small reserved pool vs hosted with burst.
[02:40] Tamara Okoye: also SSO/SCIM: we need to map RBAC roles, who gets access to logs, and how long logs are retained, especially for audit.
[02:50] Jordan Lee: default is 90 days for request traces in the hosted plan but with dedicated and enterprise you can extend retention. logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or S3 push, and audit events are available when you enable enterprise audit logging.
[03:05] Priya Patel: ok, for now we need ability to export to our S3 bucket and have access limited to a security group.
[03:10] Maya Chen: noted. we'll include the export walkthrough.
[03:16] Luis Ramirez: back to creds: we tried the service account with the initial key and saw 403 for the gateway, error says 'invalid audience' which is probably the JWT aud, can you share the audience string?
[03:28] Jordan Lee: yes, it's service.redwood-api.orionfin.staging, i'll paste exact string in the slack thread. also ensure the token header has kid referencing the vault key.
[03:40] Priya Patel: perfect.
[03:42] Maya Chen: action item: we'll produce a 1-page runbook for gateway setup and common TLS fixes, plus a checklist for KMS and audit — target EOD friday.
[03:55] Tamara Okoye: sounds good.
[04:00] Priya Patel: on benchmarks: can we schedule a 2-hour perf window where you run tail-latency microbench with KV warming? we have a staging window next tuesday morning.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: yes we can do that, we'd like to coordinate exact traffic profile, token lengths, and the prompt set. we can also run between 08:00-10:00 UTC on 2026-08-04.
[04:22] Luis Ramirez: works for us. we'll provide sample payloads and a matching prometheus scrape for metrics collection.
[04:30] Maya Chen: great. a few quick clarifications — will the traffic be routed through your firewall NAT? sometimes source IP impacts our connection pool size and keepalive tuning.
[04:44] Luis Ramirez: yes, it will. we'll send the firewall egress ranges.
[04:48] Jordan Lee: for the run we'll enable KV cache, set batch sizes to 8 and max tokens to 512 to mirror production; if you prefer we can try batch 4 first to hit lower tail latency.
[05:05] Priya Patel: run both if possible, give us results side-by-side.
[05:10] Maya Chen: noted.
[05:12] Tamara Okoye: final question: data retention and deletion policy? when we send user PII, how long is it kept?
[05:20] Jordan Lee: by default hosted short term logs are kept for 90 days but we have configurable retention for enterprise and private where you can set zero retention on logs and only store model inputs transiently. plus redwood doesn't use PII for training, we can sign off in the DPA.
[05:36] Priya Patel: ok great, that's important.
[05:40] Maya Chen: to close, recap — Redwood to share SOC2/KMS notes, runbook, audience string; customer to finish vault role, provide gateway allowlist and firewall egress, and confirm staging perf window 08:00-10:00 UTC 2026-08-04. we'll meet next week same time for results review.
[05:58] Priya Patel: thanks all.
[06:00] meeting end
